candidates.title: PRT player turns any one-time error while building a uarch claim into a permanent refusal to join that inner tournament for the life of the process (try_new_uarch_tree + failed_uarch_periods)
candidates.component: PRT player in doc/recipes (prt.lua event_handler.commit_uarch_claim, try_new_uarch_tree), run by crisium.lua through prt-bridge.lua build_claim
candidates.role: Support (AUDIT.md: 'The PRT player and bridge in doc/recipes ... Support'), standing in for the honest operator (THREAT_MODEL section 3: 'implementations of an operator that no deployment runs')
candidates.location: doc/recipes/prt.lua:1918-1950 (try_new_uarch_tree = util.protect(...); commit_uarch_claim records self.failed_uarch_periods[period_key] = true and returns "nothing" on every later call); doc/recipes/prt-bridge.lua:219-262, 300-330 (build_claim is retried every tick while the child is joinable, but each retry hits the failed_uarch_periods short-circuit); crisium.lua main loop never relaunches the process for it (only an uncaught error crashes it).
candidates.description: commit_uarch_claim wraps the whole uarch claim build (new_machine_pair_at_epoch_input_offset -> clone_stored/load/commit of pair/ and pair.revert, replay of inputs, collect_uarch_cycle_root_hashes, forest building) in util.protect. Any error, whatever its cause, is converted into an anomaly ('uarch_error', reported once) and the (input, period) key is stored in self.failed_uarch_periods, an in-memory table that is never cleared. From then on every call for that period returns "nothing" without trying again. The bridge's build_claim is called again on every tick while the inner tournament is joinable, so a later attempt would succeed once the cause is gone, but it never runs. The bridge then never joins that child tournament with the honest uarch claim. In Dave, the inner tournament is won by the opponent's uarch claim alone, and the honest mcycle claim loses its match. The comment frames the failure as deterministic ('fails when the uarch run of some mcycle ... trapped or reached its maximum cycle'), which R3/R4 say never happens from a reachable state. So in practice the only errors that reach this path are transient ones: ENOSPC or EIO while cloning or syncing pair/ and pair.revert, which costs two full-machine clones and syncs per build, EMFILE, ENOMEM inside a collection, or a lock conflict. A crash would instead have relaunched the player under prt-supervise.sh, which retries.
candidates.trigger: No adversary data is needed. A transient host condition during the one uarch claim build that a dispute forces (an adversary can steer the dispute so the build happens at any time, for example while the disk is temporarily full with the open epoch's inputs, entries, pair clones and forests). The condition then clears.
candidates.reachability: Reachable on the honest operator's path whenever the build raises once. Every mcycle match that ends at a leaf opens an inner tournament, and the honest player must build a uarch claim there. No deterministic error is known from a reachable state. The defect needs an error that happens once and would not happen again.
rating_steps: 1. Out of scope? The trigger is a host fault. Section 8 excludes 'Host faults, such as a full disk, as long as the emulator does not turn them into a wrong hash, a wrong proof, or a directory that O2 guarantees but that later loads as a different state', and section 4 says 'A host fault ... may stop the honest operator'. Here the player does not stop. It keeps running and gives up the claim for good. The outcome is neither a wrong hash nor a wrong proof, so a literal reading of the exclusion puts it Out of scope. Under the other reading, R4 requires that 'After a stop, it restarts from a directory that O2 guarantees and keeps defending its claim'. A host fault may stop the operator, but here it does not stop: the fault becomes a lasting refusal to defend the claim, which a restart would have avoided. On that reading the exclusion does not apply.

2. Role: AUDIT.md rates the PRT player as Support ('No production deployment runs the player'). Section 3: 'A defect that only a support component shows is Medium when it would rate High or Critical in the role the component stands in for, such as ... the honest operator for an implementation of an operator'.

3. High/Medium cases: none of the High cases fits ('caused by data from other parties' does not apply). In the stood-in honest role the effect is a Completeness failure (section 1: the honest operator 'cannot respond in time. If the honest claim is eliminated, a dishonest claim can win'). Capped at Medium for support.

4. Critical (stood-in role): R4 'The honest operator ... submits its transactions within the dispute clocks. After a stop, it restarts ... and keeps defending its claim', and section 1's completeness failure. This would be Critical for the honest operator under the second reading of step 1, so Medium for this support component.
5. Otherwise Low: if the host-fault exclusion is read literally, the defect is Out of scope, or Low as a robustness defect of a support tool.
candidates.claimed_severity: Medium (reading B: a host fault turned into a lasting failure to defend, not a stop) / Out of scope (reading A: literal host-fault exclusion)
candidates.threat_to_goal: In the stood-in honest role, a recoverable condition removes the honest claim from the uarch-level tournament it must win. The honest mcycle claim is then eliminated and a dishonest claim can settle (section 1, completeness failure). Neither crashing, which the supervisor relaunches, nor retrying while the joining window is open would lose the claim.
candidates.evidence: Code reading only. prt.lua:1934-1943 store the failure in self.failed_uarch_periods and return "nothing" with no retry path. The table is not persisted, so only a process relaunch clears it, and crisium relaunches only on an uncaught error. prt-bridge.lua:309-330 call build_claim on every tick while can_join holds. Each call reaches the short-circuit at prt.lua:1936. No experiment run.
candidates.test_idea: Load prt.lua as a module, open a stored player on a small epoch, and seal it. Wrap player.new_uarch_tree (or machine:clone_stored) so that the first call raises a simulated ENOSPC error and later calls succeed. Call event_handler.commit_uarch_claim(player, i, p) twice. The required behavior is that the second call returns a claim (or that the first call raises, so the supervisor relaunches the player). The test fails (exit 1) while the second call returns "nothing".

inventory_summary: prt.lua player side: every assert and error() was listed and classified by who controls its inputs. Guest-controlled: receive_cmio_request cmd assert (unreachable: break reasons YIELDED_MANUALLY/AUTOMATICALLY imply the matching tohost cmd); mcycle/uarch bundle-capacity asserts and pad-bundle/final-bundle consistency asserts (checked against machine.cpp collect_mcycle_root_hashes, including final_bundle_sibling_hashes set at a non-fixed-point collection end, fixed point at entry, rejected-yield sample hash); 'input stopped outside a fixed point' (unreachable: imcyclemax = base + 2^48 - 1 < mcycle_end, overflow checked before target even when saturated); rollback hash asserts (revert_root_hash always equals the boundary hash: set at creation and at each accepted yield, unchanged by rejections and stops). Chain/listener-controlled: add_pending_input ordering/limit/history asserts, epoch_sealed count assert, prt-epoch seal asserts (all already candidates or consistent with DaveConsensus). Peer-steered positions: reveal_bisection/seal_divergence/commit_uarch_claim/prove_state_transition at empty slots past input_count, slots after an epoch stop, periods after a rejection inside the same input, the rejecting mcycle and the mcycle after it, saturated mcycles. Traced by hand and found consistent. Tables indexed by peer data: self.trees[computation_hash] (keyed only by the honest bridge's own claim roots), failed_uarch_periods, uarch_claims dedupe. Stored files: state.json, machine-cache, forests, last-output, epoch.json (trusted under O2; asserts only).

hash-tree.lua: ran randomized differential tests against naive trees. frontier push/append/pad_back/get_root_hash: 9000 trials over 3 seeds, 0 failures. frontier_forest append/push/pad (raw and forest values, repeated blocks), get_node_hash, get_siblings, expand_leaf, store/load/re-store: about 2700 trials, heights 1-7. The only failure class was 'leaf height mismatch' on expand_leaf after store/load when equal-hash subtrees have different base heights. That is R4-RGPROOF-1, not re-reported. Node hashes and siblings were always correct or allowed-opaque.

crisium.lua/prt-epoch.lua/prt-command.lua/prt-supervise.sh: asserts and I/O read. Nothing new beyond R1-A3-1, R2-DFINPUTCOUNT-2, R1-BOUNDARY-3, R4-RGEPOCHS-2 and R4-RGPLAYERGUEST-2. fs.clone_file falls back to a copy on EXDEV, so a temporary input file on another filesystem is fine.
not_covered: No end-to-end run of crisium + bridge on the local chain, and no player-restart runner. Everything above is code reading, plus the Lua-level hash-tree fuzzers.
prt-bridge.lua, prt-ethereum.lua, prt-transactions.lua, prt-log-history.lua (only their calls into the player were read).
The referee side of prt.lua and prtu.lua's transport and schema decoding (the referee model, not the player).
Forked (non-stored) player paths: JSON-RPC fork_server/rebind/swap failure behavior.

frontier_forest fuzzing at heights above 7, and with forest values deeper than one level of nesting. Lazy loading of children across several store generations with crash-leftover tree files (beyond confirming the R4-RGPROOF-1 class).
Power-loss injection on the stored epoch directory, entries, agreed pair and checkpoints (reasoned only; earlier O2 candidates cover the known cases).
Released geometry (log2 period 18) cost of building a uarch claim, opening bundles, and the clone-per-pair cost of the stored cache (R12/A7, covered by earlier candidates).
cartesi-machine.lua's uses of hash-tree.lua (CLI computation hashes), outside this angle beyond the frontier fuzz.
